title: crossbeam-candidate-prio-inversion-causing-hidden-kv-garbage
creator: Ava Chen
description: Intermittent token-level corruption and slight numerical drift observed after enabling the experimental crossbeam speculative coalescer. Investigation points to a priority inversion in kernel candidate selection which allowed stale KV cache entries to be read during decode, producing silent softmax shifts and rare duplicated tokens. This ticket coordinates debugging, temporary mitigations, and the definitive fix to ensure atomic ownership transfers and safe reclamation.
reproduction_steps: Start the local inference harness with model 'redwood-3b-quant' and set CROSSBEAM=1
Run an 8-beam prefill followed by alternating decode with variable-length prompts (mean 120, stdev 30)
Execute 1000 concurrent small requests with batch sizes ranging 1-4 and pinned CPU/GPU affinity across two worker threads
Monitor logs for 'kv_read_unexpected_len' and token anomalies; failures typically appear after ~2000 requests on mixed-precision-enabled hosts
Disable CROSSBEAM to confirm regression disappears

root_cause: The speculative crossbeam coalescer can leave a preempted low-priority kernel marked as the owner of a KV slot while a higher-priority candidate reuses that same slot. Because the candidate->slot updates and eviction notifications were not performed atomically with proper release/acquire fences, a brief window allows reads to return stale tensor contents. Combined with AMP rounding, this leads to silent numerical drift and occasional token corruption.

mitigations: hotfix-1: disable crossbeam speculative coalescer via CROSSBEAM=0 for hosted clusters (eliminates correctness issue at cost of throughput)
hotfix-2: add short quiescence window after eviction to block reads until mapping confirmation (temporary; increases latency)
long-term: implement atomic CAS ownership transfer for KV slots and add memory fences around handoff/evict paths
fix_proposal: Introduce CAS-based ownership transfer for KV slot descriptors (atomic 64-bit descriptor)
Add memory_order_release on handoff writes and memory_order_acquire on cache reads in C++ runtime code paths
Update scheduler to synchronously complete handoff when a high-priority candidate will reuse a slot
Add unit tests simulating interleaved prefill/decode scheduling and a fuzz harness for mixed-precision race windows
Add e2e regression test in CI with crossbeam enabled and fixed RNG seed to detect behavioral drift
